messages.author: bef64eec421ae34f
messages.subject: unknown error using the poppr function
parts:
Dear

I have been using poppr for a while now, and experienced an unknown error when I tried to use the poppr function on a genind object:


-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
Pop     = Population name (Total == Pooled)
N       = Census population size
MLG     = Number of unique multilocus genotypes (MLG) observed
eMLG    = Number of expected MLG based on rarefaction at smallest N >= 10
SE      = Standard error of rarefaction analysis
H       = Shannon-Wiener Index of MLG diversity
G       = Stoddart and Taylor's Index of MLG diversity
lambda  = Simpson's index
E.5     = Evenness
Hexp    = Nei's 1978 expected heterozygosity
Ia      = Index of association
rbarD   = Standardized index of association
-------------------------------------------------------------------------|

Error in if (any(object@ploidy < 1L)) { : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In validityMethod(object) :
  @tab does not contain integers; as of adegenet_2.0-0, numeric values are no longer used
2: In validityMethod(object) :
  @tab does not contain integers; as of adegenet_2.0-0, numeric values are no longer used
3: In validityMethod(object) :
  @tab does not contain integers; as of adegenet_2.0-0, numeric values are no longer used




Below is the code I used, and the sessionInfo().

Thanks in advance for your help,
Emmanuel

The code:

#Importation
eth17<-read.delim("ethiopia2017_withGroups.txt",header=T, sep="\t", row.names=1)

#conversion to a genind object
e.st1<-df2genind(eth17[,1:19],pop=as.factor(eth17[,44]), ploidy=1, ncode=2,NA.char="NA", type="codom")
e.st1$other<-eth17[,20:51]
e.st1$other$xy<-eth17[,c(42,43)]

#Defining strata
strata(e.st1)<-data.frame(other(e.st1))[c("gr.geo4","gr.alt2","STRUCT1")]

# And change the names so we know what they are
nameStrata(e.st1) <-~Region/Altitude/location


##poppr
library(poppr)

resume<-poppr(e.st1,missing="mean",method=1, sample=9999,minsamp=5,strata=~Region/location, plot=T, legend=T)

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] unknown error using the poppr function
parts:
I believe I have found the culprit. It appears that sample 85 has not been assigned a population. This uncovered a bug for this particular case in the adegenet code, which I will go ahead and open an issue for. In the mean time, I would suggest that you do the following:

1. When you import your data, set stringsAsFactors = FALSE in your read.delim() call.
2. Replace the NA values of your population columns to something human-readable like "?"

Once you have that, then your data will run again.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

Le mercredi 30 mai 2018 23:00:38 UTC+2, Zhian Kamvar a écrit :
I believe I have found the culprit. It appears that sample 85 has not been assigned a population. This uncovered a bug for this particular case in the adegenet code, which I will go ahead and open an issue for. In the mean time, I would suggest that you do the following:

1. When you import your data, set stringsAsFactors = FALSE in your read.delim() call.
2. Replace the NA values of your population columns to something human-readable like "?"

Once you have that, then your data will run again.

Hope that helps,
Zhian

Zhian
